_note: Transfer (stamp) duty for residential purchases in each state and territory, 2026-27. One source of truth: build.py renders the rate tables and state pages from this file, and the calculator reads it from the page. Bracket: 'to' = top of the band (null = no limit); duty = base + rate x (value - over) / 100, or 'flat' = % of the whole value. 'round': 'part' = each rate applies per $100 or part of $100; 'exact' = straight percentage. Check every state each July (NSW indexes thresholds every 1 July) and after state budgets. Record changes in CLAIMS.md.

NSW.name: New South Wales
NSW.general_note: Thresholds apply to contracts from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027. The top band is premium property duty on residential land.
NSW.fhb_short: No duty up to $800,000; reduced up to $1 million
NSW.fhb_text: Under the First Home Buyers Assistance Scheme, eligible first home buyers pay no transfer duty on a new or existing home valued up to $800,000, and a reduced amount up to $1,000,000. For vacant land to build a first home, there's no duty up to $350,000 and a reduced amount up to $450,000. You need to move in within 12 months and live there for at least 12 months.
NSW.surcharge: Surcharge purchaser duty for foreign buyers (an extra 9% of the value)

fhog.text: The First Home Owner (New Homes) Grant pays $10,000 towards a new, off-the-plan or substantially renovated home priced up to $600,000, or a land and building contract up to $750,000 combined. There's no grant for established homes.

VIC.name: Victoria
VIC.general_note: General rates for contracts from 1 July 2021, which also apply to investment properties.
VIC.owner_title: Principal place of residence rates (homes valued up to $550,000)
VIC.fhb_short: No duty up to $600,000; reduced up to $750,000
VIC.fhb_text: Eligible first home buyers pay no duty on a home valued up to $600,000, and a reduced amount up to $750,000. Separately, if you'll live in the home, the principal place of residence concession lowers the rates on homes valued up to $550,000.
VIC.surcharge: Foreign purchaser additional duty (an extra 8% of the value)

fhog.text: The First Home Owner Grant pays $10,000 towards buying or building a new home valued up to $750,000. There's no grant for established homes.

QLD.name: Queensland
QLD.general_note: General rates, which apply to investment properties.
QLD.owner_title: Home concession rates (a home you'll live in)
QLD.fhb_short: No duty on a new home; established homes up to $700,000
QLD.fhb_text: First home buyers of an established home can claim a concession that removes duty on homes valued up to $700,000, reducing in steps until it ends at $800,000. Since 1 May 2025, first home buyers of a new home, or vacant land to build one, can claim a full concession with no price cap. From 1 August 2026, home concessions are generally only available to Australian citizens, permanent residents and specified foreign retirees. The $30,000 First Home Owner Grant continues for eligible new homes valued under $750,000.
QLD.surcharge: Additional foreign acquirer duty (an extra 8% of the value)
QLD.grant: You may also be eligible for Queensland's $30,000 First Home Owner Grant for new homes under $750,000.

fhog.text: The First Home Owner Grant pays $30,000 towards buying or building a new home valued under $750,000, including land. The Queensland Government has confirmed it continues for eligible contracts signed from 1 July 2026. There's no grant for established homes.

WA.name: Western Australia
WA.general_note: WA uses the same general rates for home buyers and investors.
WA.fhb_short: No duty up to $600,000; reduced up to $800,000
WA.fhb_text: For transactions from 7 May 2026, eligible first home buyers pay no duty on a home valued up to $600,000, and a concessional rate ($16.15 per $100 above $600,000) up to $800,000. For vacant land to build a first home, there's no duty up to $450,000, with a concession up to $550,000.
WA.surcharge: Foreign transfer duty (an extra 7% of the value)

fhog.text: The First Home Owner Grant pays $10,000 towards buying or building a new home. For transactions from 7 May 2026, the home can be valued up to $800,000 south of the 26th parallel, which includes Perth, or $1,000,000 further north. There's no grant for established homes.

SA.name: South Australia
SA.general_note: SA uses the same rates for home buyers and investors.
SA.fhb_short: No duty on a new home; none on established homes
SA.fhb_text: For contracts from 6 June 2024, eligible first home buyers pay no stamp duty on a new home, an off-the-plan apartment or vacant land to build a home, with no price cap. There's no first home buyer concession on an established home.
SA.surcharge: The foreign ownership surcharge (an extra 7% of the value)

fhog.short: Up to $15,000 on a new home
fhog.text: The First Home Owner Grant pays up to $15,000 towards buying or building a new home, including an off-the-plan apartment or a substantially renovated home, with no cap on its value. There's no grant for established homes.

TAS.name: Tasmania
TAS.general_note: Tasmania uses the same rates for every buyer.
TAS.fhb_short: No concession (the established-home exemption ended 30 June 2026)
TAS.fhb_text: Tasmania's duty exemption for first home buyers of established homes ended for transfers settling after 30 June 2026, so first home buyers now pay the standard rates.
TAS.surcharge: The foreign investor duty surcharge (an extra 8% of the value)

fhog.text: For transactions that start between 1 July 2026 and 30 June 2027, the First Home Owner Grant is $20,000 towards building or buying a new home, with no cap on its value. It's set to return to $10,000 after that.

ACT.name: Australian Capital Territory
ACT.general_note: Rates for buyers who won't live in the property (investors).
ACT.fhb_short: No duty if you haven't owned property in five years
ACT.fhb_text: From 1 July 2026, the Home Buyer Concession Scheme removes duty for eligible buyers, with no income test or price cap. You and your partner can't have owned property in the last five years, and you need to live in the home. It covers new homes, established homes and vacant residential land. Owner-occupiers who aren't eligible pay the lower owner-occupier rates.
ACT.surcharge_none: The ACT doesn't add a foreign purchaser surcharge to conveyance duty.

fhog.text: The ACT doesn't offer a first home owner grant. Help comes through the Home Buyer Concession Scheme on duty instead.

NT.name: Northern Territory
NT.general_note: The NT uses the same rates for every buyer.
NT.fhb_short: No duty concession; grants and a house and land exemption
NT.fhb_text: The Northern Territory has no general first home buyer duty concession. A stamp duty exemption applies to eligible house and land packages for contracts signed between 1 July 2022 and 30 June 2027, and first home buyers may be eligible for grants. Check the Territory Revenue Office for current eligibility.
NT.surcharge_none: The NT doesn't charge a foreign purchaser surcharge on stamp duty.

fhog.text: The HomeGrown Territory Grant pays $50,000 to first home buyers who build or buy a new home, including off the plan, with no cap on the price. Contracts need to be signed between 1 October 2024 and 30 September 2027. The $10,000 grant for established homes has closed.
